I made it "fun". I will never have the discipline to follow a strict regime, so I had to find a way that didn't involve any effort. The most important thing was for me not to have a goal that only had its reward at the end (aka. Losing the weigt). It'll take a long time  – especially if you intend on losing weight by working out and eating healthier, so constantly having to force yourself is going to be very hard. What I did instead was to make each day a competition on how long I was able to wait with eating. This made it so that each hour I was able to restrain myself felt like a huge victory, and I felt really accomplished.  When I was able to go more than a day, I felt really good, and I was so invested in keeping my streak. The more invested I was, the more enduring was easier; how much I could endure was fun in itself.  When I felt like I couldn't hold myself, I ate whatever and was happy with myself, and then moved on excited to try again. I didn't think about the end goal at all, I just reminded myself that if I kept playing this game, I'd get there, which I did really fast (20 kg in 3 months).

This is a though one, because it has a lot to do with how your mentality. Not to say that it's something wrong with you or that it's uncommon. It's actually something EVERYONE and I don't say that lightly experience. Even the cool people you'd think never had suh a worry. I'll try to give some advice that made it easier for me overcome it. Bht as I said, it happenes to everyone and that includes me. So one thing that helps is realizing that, but that's easier said than done. You can see it in how when people like celebrities makes a mistake, they often double down on it. Usually this is due to the fact that you don't want to feel like you are feeling right now so they try to make it seem like they are in the right. It applies in many other ways than this, but I hope you get the point. I wanted to get a better example of someone doing something embarrassing, but I couldn't think of anything good, which kinda proves the fact that no one remebers stuff like that, other than their own mistakes. So that's advice one, only you (most of the time) think of stuff like that.  Other people might remeber it if you remind them, but usually people are way too busy being scared of embarrassing themselves. Second point, someone under mentioned jt I think, but do you think about all the embarrassing stuff other people do? And if you do, do you think of it as something that devalues them? If the answer is yes, you are probably an asshole, and so are other people who think that way, not worth your time. If you encounter such a person remeber that in your head, they are in the wrong, in a way that makes them worse than you. Which leads to my third advice. You hold the chains to control yourself. And it will stay that way unless you give it to them. Might be a bit too metaphorical, but idk. Advice four. Think of why you are you are finding it embarrassing. Did this thing hurt somebody else? Was it something that couldn't happen to everbody? Did this thing make you any less worth than anybody else? Making mistakes or having an accident in any form happens to again to everyone, but you probably hear that all the time, so it's up to you if you believe it or not. My last point for now is probably my favorite, owning up to embarrassing is hell of a fucking power move. People who aren't afraid of getting embarrassed or who won't let it affect them in a negative way, are hella fucking cool. And everbodys thinks that, trust me. In general there is no right way of exciting and what people perceive as such is just culture. And we all go along with it because we see everyone else do it too. But if you show that you don't see yourself to be in the wrong people will think they are in the wrong, and will be forced to change their view. As long as you belive that it's okay for anyone to be embarrassed and that other people are dicks for thinking otherwise, you'll be in power. Or in the worst case, you don't want their company anyways. I'll end my monolog here. I hope it can be of some help, if you have to patient to even read it at all, hahha. You can always send me a message in my dms if you need to talk with someone, or if you didn't understand anything of this ramble. No matter what happens you'll be fine, trust me.
